rationale:
Evidence: iteration 3 (685.6, best so far) keeps oval at 100% finish and s-bend at 85%. Slalom still never finishes (0/20, progress 0.585, max_error 0.065, 1.25 line-loss events), and every slalom run leaves the track. Iteration 1 showed that widening the sensor array was the change that most improved slalom progress (0.12 to 0.39), and line-loss events fell as coverage grew. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit, because the 0.06 m floor binds across the whole body range. Iteration 2 showed that raising kp to 4.5 hurt the oval and s-bend, so I keep kp near 4.0 in effect.

Changes: (1) Extend the array from 5 to 7 sensors at x = -0.045 to +0.045 m in 15 mm steps. This keeps the tape visible at lateral errors near 0.05 m, which is the slalom excursion range, and should cut line-loss events. (2) Rescale the weights to x/0.0225, giving [-2, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2]. The outer sensors therefore still reach the ±2 limit. (3) Raise kp to 6.0 so the inner-sensor steering gain stays at about the iteration 3 level (4.0 x 1.5 x 0.667 = 4.0). Outer-sensor gain rises modestly, which should help recovery from larger excursions. Mass 0.6, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.5, sensor size 16 mm, line_loss last_direction and the y position of 0.05 m are kept unchanged, so the effect of the array change is isolated as far as possible.

Expected result: slalom line-loss events fall below 0.5, slalom progress rises above 0.6, and some slalom runs finish. Oval completion should hold at 100%. Hypotheses: (a) the wider 7-sensor array reduces line loss on slalom; (b) the matched kp keeps s-bend and oval behaviour close to iteration 3; (c) steering_oscillation stays at or below 0.35. Measurements wanted: per-track completion, max_error and line_loss_events on slalom, and steering_oscillation on all tracks.
